mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, if you're standing in the wake of loss, I want you to remember—this journey isn't straightforward, and there are no shortcuts through grief. The Year of Magical Thinking doesn't promise easy solutions, but it lights the way with honesty, compassion, and the kind of wisdom that's earned, not given. It's not just a story about getting through loss, but about learning to live alongside it—finding meaning, connection, and even sparks of hope, right in the heart of sorrow. So, what can you take away from all this? Grief isn't something you can predict or control. It comes in waves, sometimes gentle, sometimes overwhelming, never quite following any rules. That urge for magical thinking—that wish to somehow undo the past—is more common than you might think. It's just your heart's way of handling the impossible. Everyday routines can sting, but they can also comfort. And while reaching out to others truly matters, sometimes even the most caring support has its limits, and that's okay. Healing doesn't mean leaving the past behind—it means weaving your loss into the story of who you are now. If you catch yourself searching for answers, replaying old memories, or feeling alone in your grief, know that these aren’t signs of weakness—they’re signs of love. Give yourself permission to move at your own pace. Accept help when it comes. Honor what you've lost in ways that feel right to you. Some days, the pain might feel like too much. Other days, hope will quietly slip back in. Trust that both have their place. In time, you’ll find you can carry your loss with a kind of grace, discover joy right alongside sorrow, and build a future that cherishes what’s come before. This journey is yours—and you don’t have to walk it alone.
